<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

VS Code should provide a setting that disables the GitHub Copilot Agent Host provider without disabling the Chat feature or other Agent Host providers.

A setting consistent with the existing provider settings would be:

```jsonc
{
  "chat.agentHost.copilotAgent.enabled": false
}
```

The existing settings provide this control for Claude and Codex:

```jsonc
{
  "chat.agentHost.claudeAgent.enabled": true,
  "chat.agentHost.codexAgent.enabled": true
}
```

There is currently no equivalent setting for Copilot.

## Problem

I use the Codex Agent Host provider with my OpenAI subscription. I do not use GitHub Copilot models.

I have hidden all Copilot models in Manage Language Models. However, Copilot still appears in Chat and the model selector still displays unavailable Copilot models, sign-in prompts, and upgrade actions.

Model visibility therefore does not disable the Copilot provider itself.

The existing alternatives do not solve this:

- `chat.disableAIFeatures` disables the complete Chat feature, including providers I want to use.
- Hiding Copilot models does not remove the provider or unavailable featured models.
- Disabling Copilot autocomplete-related features does not remove the Agent Host provider.
- There is no `chat.agentHost.copilotAgent.enabled` equivalent to the Claude and Codex settings.
- The former global `chat.agentHost.enabled` setting was removed and would have been too broad in any case.

## Requested behavior

When `chat.agentHost.copilotAgent.enabled` is `false`:

1. Do not register or advertise the Copilot/Copilot CLI Agent Host provider.
2. Do not offer Copilot as a provider or harness for new Chat sessions.
3. Remove Copilot-hosted models from Chat model selectors.
4. Do not display Copilot-specific unavailable models, sign-in prompts, upgrade actions, quota messages, or model promotions in Chat.
5. Keep the general Chat feature enabled.
6. Keep Codex, Claude, BYOK, and third-party Agent Host providers available.
7. Preserve existing Copilot sessions without deleting user data. They can remain readable when explicitly opened, but Copilot should not be offered for new sessions.
8. Preserve the current behavior when the setting is absent or `true`.

Requiring a window reload after changing the setting would be acceptable if provider registration occurs during Agent Host startup.

## Scope

This request targets the Chat and Agent Host provider system.

The following features are out of scope and can continue to use their existing controls:

- Inline completions
- Next-edit suggestions
- Commit-message generation
- Code review
- Other Copilot features that are not implemented through Agent Host

This request also does not ask for a global opt-out from promotions for every model provider. It only asks that Copilot-specific UI disappear when the Copilot provider is explicitly disabled.

## Steps demonstrating the current behavior

1. Enable the Codex Agent Host provider.
2. Open Manage Language Models.
3. Hide every GitHub Copilot model.
4. Open Chat and its model or provider selector.
5. Observe that Copilot-related entries and upgrade affordances are still present.
6. Try to disable only the Copilot provider.
7. Observe that no supported provider-level setting exists.

## Related work

- [#321155](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/321155) added `chat.agentHost.claudeAgent.enabled` and `chat.agentHost.codexAgent.enabled`, but no Copilot equivalent.
- [#331464](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/331464) notes that no per-provider Copilot toggle currently exists, but that issue primarily concerns authentication.
- [#320213](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/320213) requested hiding upgrade-only Copilot models, but was closed without implementation.
- [#330934](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/330934) requests a broader opt-out from model promotional notifications.
- [#329303](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/329303) removed the global Agent Host rollout setting, making provider-specific controls more important.

title: multiDiffEditor: fix: preserve live document state across refreshes
body:
## Problem

In the Agents window's Branch Changes editor, a file could expand after the user had collapsed it. Scrolling only revealed the reset: the state changed earlier when marking a file as Viewed triggered a live changeset refresh.

The shared multi-diff widget retained the originally restored per-document state indefinitely. Whenever the document list changed, it rebuilt `VirtualizedViewItem` wrappers and reapplied that original snapshot—even when the underlying `DocumentDiffItemViewModel` was still the same live object. A stale `collapsed: false` value could therefore overwrite a newer user-selected `collapsed: true` value.

## Fix

This change treats persisted document state as one-time bootstrap state rather than continuously enforced state:

- Restore each `DocumentDiffItemViewModel` at most once.
- Maintain a write-through cache of the latest collapse and modified-editor selection state.
- Bootstrap genuinely recreated view models from that latest state.
- Preserve the last known selection when an editor is temporarily unavailable during virtualization or disposal.
- Guard cache writes by the current multi-diff model so disposed wrappers cannot contaminate a replacement model.
- Clear restoration state when installing a model without view state.
- Initialize a pooled editor with the restored selection—or `(1,1)` when none exists—before publishing it to observers.

This preserves current user interaction across additive resource refreshes while still supporting delayed documents and remove/re-add scenarios.

## Deliberate behavior

Repeated `setViewState` calls for the same model no longer overwrite newer live state, including state for temporarily absent documents. The first state replaces the cache; later calls only seed previously unseen document keys.

A replacement model starts clean unless it is explicitly given view state, even when it contains the same original/modified URI pairs as the previous model.

## Tests

Added real-widget browser regressions covering:

- An additive document-list refresh retaining current collapse and selection state.
- A delayed document receiving persisted state once, then retaining user changes.
- Forced virtualization and pooled-editor reuse without cross-document selection transfer.
- A document without saved selection receiving the editor default instead of recycled state.
- Remove/repeated-restore/re-add view-model recreation restoring the latest live state.
- Replacement-model isolation and late explicit restoration.

## Validation

title: agentHost: log shadowed Claude customizations in multi-root workspaces
body:
Fixes #331508

## Problem

In a multi-root workspace, when two folders each contribute a standalone **skill** (or custom **agent**) with the **same name**, first-name-wins discovery keeps the primary folder's copy and drops the other. Because the Claude SDK/CLI exposes standalone skills/agents by name only (no source-scoped identity like `plugin:skill`), the shadowed copy is **unreachable by any name** — and it was previously dropped **with no diagnostic**.

This matches the issue's minimum expected behavior: *"or at minimum some indication that a discovered customization was shadowed."*

## Change (log-only; discovery output unchanged)

- `selectFirstClaudeCustomizationByKey` gains an optional `onShadowed(shadowed, winner)` callback, invoked for each later item dropped by the first-name-wins merge. Return value and precedence are unchanged; the `.has()` claim check is preserved so the helper stays safe for any future caller.
- The multi-root discovery path passes a callback that logs a `warn` for each shadowed agent/skill:
  ```
  [claudeMultiRootCustomizationDiscovery] skill 'deploy' at '<uri-B>' is shadowed by '<uri-A>' from another workspace folder and is unreachable by name
  ```
- Same-named **user-scope** (`~/.claude`) copies are excluded by object identity, so ordinary project-over-user precedence stays quiet. Using identity (not path containment) keeps this correct even when a workspace folder lives under the home directory.

Only the multi-root branch is affected; single-root project/user precedence is unchanged and matches the Claude CLI. This is a diagnostic — the shadowed copy remains unreachable by name at the SDK level (verified against the Claude CLI), so this surfaces the collision rather than silently discarding it. A scoped-name / disambiguation solution would require SDK support and is out of scope here.

## Docs

- `src/vs/sessions/AI_CUSTOMIZATIONS.md` — documented the new diagnostic and the user-scope exclusion.

## Test

- Added a regression test in `claudeMultiRootCustomizationDiscovery.test.ts`: a workspace-vs-workspace **skill** and **agent** collision each warn exactly once, and a same-named **user-scope** copy produces no warning.

## Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/customizations/claudeMultiRootCustomizationDiscovery.test.ts` — 5 passing (new test + existing precedence/dedup/single-root parity).
- `npm run typecheck-client` — clean.

Refs #331067, #321651

title: Apply multi-diff options before attaching models
body:
tl;dr: I was debugging a window hang when I open a certain session. The session had a changed file which was minified with very long lines. Based on logs and traces, it appears that the multi-diff editor was rendering with a slower accessibility-friendly wrapping mode, but I did not have accessibility mode enabled. Looks like the option is not properly passed into the multi-diff editor. 

> fell back to Electron's native signal

I don't understand this part, why Electron is reporting that accessibility mode should be enabled 🤷 

## Problem

`MultiDiffEditorInput` resolves the correct resource-scoped `editor` and `diffEditor` configuration for each file, but `DiffEditorItemTemplate` attached the file models before applying those options. Attaching a model immediately constructs its editor view model and computes line wrapping, so the first construction ran with the diff editor's initial/default options instead of the user's configured options.

This becomes especially expensive when Electron reports native accessibility support as enabled while the user has explicitly configured `editor.accessibilitySupport: "off"`. Before the configured value was applied, the editor saw accessibility support as unknown, fell back to Electron's native signal, and selected the advanced DOM-based wrapping strategy. Opening an Agents changeset containing multi-megabyte generated JavaScript and CSS with very long minified lines then spent about 52 seconds in `_constructLines`, primarily in repeated `Range.getClientRects()` calls, blocking the renderer.

Although this was reproduced by switching to a remote Agent Host session, SSH transport was not the bottleneck: the remote file reads completed quickly, and the renderer stalled afterward while attaching the models. The underlying issue is shared multi-diff initialization order.

## Fix

Apply each document's editor options before calling `setDiffModel`. This ensures accessibility, wrapping, and other resource-specific settings participate in the initial view-model construction instead of taking effect only after the expensive work has already happened.

This does not disable accessibility or wrapping. It makes the initial multi-diff model attachment honor the same effective configuration that subsequent updates already use.

## Testing

Added a browser regression test that verifies:

- document options are applied before model attachment;
- `editor.accessibilitySupport: "off"` is present at attachment time; and
- the embedded editor computes accessibility support as disabled.

Also ran the related diff and multi-diff unit tests and targeted ESLint checks.

(Written by Copilot)

title: revealFileInOS may ignore the passed URI or pick additional URIs from Explorer selection depending on UI state
body:
During extension development, an issue was encountered where `commands.executeCommand('revealFileInOS', uri)` may ignore the passed URI and use the current Explorer selection instead. For example: (1) an item is selected in the Explorer view, and (2) the command is invoked without switching to another view/editor, by using an extension tree view title context menu.

In general, the provided URI argument is ignored when the Explorer View is focused, has a selection, and the provided URI is not part of that selection.

According to discussions in issues such as #110869 and #232522, `revealFileInOS` appears to be an internal command tied to the Explorer view, and extensions may be expected to implement their own revealing approach.

However, the following code was found to use `revealFileInOS` with an explicit URI, relying on it to reveal the specified resource:

* https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/extensions/copilot/src/extension/log/vscode-node/requestLogTree.ts
* https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/extensions/typescript-language-features/src/typescriptServiceClient.ts
* https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/extensions/git/src/commands.ts
* https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentPluginActions.ts
* https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/actions/chatPluginActions.ts
* https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/actions/createPluginAction.ts
* https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/aiCustomization/aiCustomizationManagement.contribution.ts

These consumers may reveal incorrect paths if an unrelated item is selected in the Explorer during execution.

It seems that one of the following approaches may be needed:

* Fix `revealFileInOS` (`getMultiSelectedResources`) so an explicitly passed URI is always respected, while preserving the existing multi-selection behavior where needed.
* Change the listed consumers to avoid `revealFileInOS` and instead use a revealing mechanism that operates directly on the specified URI.
* Introduce a separate command for revealing explicitly specified URIs that is independent of Explorer selection and view focus state, also accessible by extensions.

- VS Code Version: 1.134.0
- OS Version: Windows Server 2025 26100.33296

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Install VSCode with both "Open with Code" options enabled
2. Right click in a folder in Windows Explorer
3. Observe a brief `Loading...` entry in the context menu underneath the "Open in Terminal" entry
4. The `Loading...` entry disappears. "Open with Code" never appears.

This is specifically a problem on Windows Server 2025. The context menu entry appears fine on Windows 11.

The issue can be reproduced on a completely fresh `Windows Server 2025 Datacenter: Azure Edition` server on Azure running build 26100.33222.

The issue occurs on both user and system installs.

The registry key `HKEY_CURRENT_USER\SOFTWARE\Classes\VSCodeContextMenu` is created. Running ProcMon, on Windows 11 I can see that key is opened by `DllHost` when the context menu is loaded, [as expected](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-explorer-command/blob/676a2a43194e5821af2642926bc0eef9f6edd13f/src/explorer_command.cc#L108). On Server 2025, no attempt is ever made to open that key, so it appears the failure is occurring before that step.

Note: this is **not a duplicate** of any issues in Windows 11. **This issue is specific to Server 2025.**
